# Attribute Controller Boot Integration Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make attribute-based controllers generated by Tusk usable through the normal application boot path without manual route registration.

**Architecture:** Integrate existing controller attributes and router registration into `ApplicationBuilder` as an explicit configurable discovery convention, retaining route callbacks and PSR escape hatches. Align the controller generator with the generated project namespace and directory conventions; do not add a second router or a request-path scan.

**Tech Stack:** PHP 8.2+, PHPUnit, existing Tusk Router/Container/ApplicationBuilder and project generator.

**Spec:** Approved design in the conversation; issue #11 `simplify-php-programming-model-with-typed-dto-and-convention-first-apis`; prior baseline `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-programming-model-dx-v1.md`.

## Global Constraints

- Preserve constructor injection and existing generic `#[Route]` behavior.
- Preserve explicit route callbacks and PSR-7/PSR-15 low-level APIs.
- Do not scan or reflect controllers on the request path.
- Keep generated routes deterministic where compilation is used.
- Do not introduce a mandatory dependency or hidden RoadRunner global.

## Review Focus

- No controllers found: boot remains valid and explicit routes still serve requests.
- Duplicate paths/methods between discovered and explicit routes: retain existing deterministic conflict behavior or fail with an actionable boot-time diagnostic.
- Invalid/unloadable controller class: fail at boot with the class/path identified, not on first request.
- Generated nested controller class: path and namespace remain consistent with Composer PSR-4 mapping.
- Persistent workers: discovery metadata is boot-time only; per-request data remains request-scoped.

---

### Task 1: Application boot discovery convention

**Files:**
- Modify: `tusk-core/src/Foundation/ApplicationBuilder.php`
- Test: `tusk-core/tests/Foundation/ApplicationBuilderTest.php`
- Reuse without modification unless a concrete gap is proven: `tusk-web/src/Router/Router.php` and current controller attributes

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes existing `Router::registerControllers(array $controllerClasses)` and existing route attributes.
- Produces `ApplicationBuilder::withControllers(string ...$directories): self`; default behavior follows `app/Controller`, and callers can pass alternate directories explicitly. This adds no opt-out flag because the default directory may be absent and treated as empty.

- [x] Add failing boot test: a controller under the generated app controller directory with `#[Controller]` and a verb attribute serves a request without a manual route callback.
- [x] Run the focused test and confirm it fails because the builder does not discover/register controllers.
- [x] Implement boot-time discovery through the existing router registration API; sort discovered class names deterministically and only scan the configured controller directories (including the default `app/Controller`). Register discovered controller classes in the container if they are not already registered.
- [x] Add tests for an empty controller directory, a prefixed route, 404 for an unknown route, coexistence with an explicit route callback, and duplicate-route diagnostics.
- [x] Run the focused builder/router tests and confirm all pass.

**Interfaces:**

- Produces generated controllers discoverable by Task 1 without manual route wiring.

### Task 3: End-to-end compatibility and docs

**Interfaces:**

- A controller may still accept `ServerRequestInterface` and return `ResponseInterface` as the PSR escape hatch.

## Execution Boundary

This plan does not implement DTO validation, generated CRUD, a generic route manifest, resilience attributes, or new typed configuration abstractions. Those require separate design and issue scope.
